instruction: Pick a font, then APPLY it: add its `importUrl` to the document <head> (or @import), and write its `stack` into the matching type token — od-font-display for headings, od-font-body for copy. A display serif (Cormorant, Libre Caslon, Baskervville) is HEADLINE-ONLY; always give it a sturdy sans for body (see pairsWith). Single-weight faces build hierarchy with SIZE, not weight. Load only the `weights` you use — every extra weight is bytes.
pairingNote: A classic strong pairing is a high-contrast serif display over a neutral sans body (e.g. cormorant + work-sans, libre-caslon-display + inter). For a single-family build, mulish / inter / general-sans all set display AND body cleanly.

fonts.name: Baskervville
fonts.description: A refined revival of Baskerville — high contrast, elegant, distinctly literary. Sets a tone of quiet, old-money authority.
fonts.notes: Single weight (400) plus a beautiful italic — build hierarchy with SIZE, not weight, and pair with a sans for body. Superb luxe display face.

fonts.name: Cormorant
fonts.description: A very high-contrast display serif with extravagant, calligraphic detail — dramatic, fashionable, and unmistakably luxury. Built for large sizes.
fonts.notes: DISPLAY ONLY — the fine strokes fall apart below ~28px. Set it big and airy for a headline; always pair with a sturdy sans for body.

fonts.name: General Sans
fonts.description: A do-everything geometric grotesque with subtly humanist terminals — modern, neutral, and slightly premium. The default "just works" sans for product UI.
fonts.notes: NOT on Google Fonts — hosted on Fontshare (free). Load via the Fontshare API href in importUrl, or self-host from fontshare.com. Used by Vesper, Obsidian Luxe, Neural Monitor, Stackside, Dringle.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.description: The definitive UI grotesque — engineered for screens, huge weight range, tall x-height, superb legibility. The safe, professional default.
fonts.notes: The most versatile body face here and a strong neutral display. Used by Creative Director and New Era. When in doubt for product UI, this.

fonts.name: Lato
fonts.description: A humanist sans with warm, semi-rounded details and a serious feel — approachable but grown-up. Excellent long-form body face.
fonts.notes: Reads beautifully at body sizes. Slightly softer and warmer than Roboto; good when you want friendly without childish.

fonts.name: Libre Caslon Display
fonts.description: A high-contrast Caslon cut for large display — sharp serifs, dramatic thick-thins, a fashion-masthead presence. Confident and editorial.
fonts.stack: 'Libre Caslon Display', ui-serif, Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif
fonts.notes: DISPLAY ONLY, single weight + italic. Reads as a magazine masthead — set large. Never for body. Pair with a neutral sans (Inter/Manrope).

fonts.name: Lora
fonts.description: A contemporary transitional serif with brushed calligraphic roots — well-balanced, warm, and highly readable in running text. Editorial without being stuffy.
fonts.notes: A rare serif that is genuinely comfortable for BODY copy, not just headlines. Its italics are lovely for pull quotes.

fonts.name: Manrope
fonts.description: A modern geometric-humanist sans with tight, semi-condensed proportions — feels engineered and premium. A favourite for SaaS and fintech.
fonts.notes: Excellent tight display headings; also a clean body. Pairs well as the sans in a serif-display / sans-body split.

fonts.name: Montserrat
fonts.description: A geometric sans inspired by old Buenos Aires signage — wide, confident, with a fashionable urban air. Shines set large and tight as a headline.
fonts.notes: Strong at display, competent at body. Track headings tight for a modern look; its wide caps love letter-spacing when set small.

fonts.name: Mulish
fonts.description: A minimalist sans with a warm, rounded skeleton — friendly but disciplined. Reads clean at every size, from oversized display to fine print.
fonts.notes: The ODORO workhorse (Clair, GringX, Lumen, Stride use it). Happy setting both display and body — a safe single-family choice.

fonts.name: Nunito
fonts.description: A rounded-terminal sans — soft, bouncy, and warm without tipping into cute. The friendliest face on this list.
fonts.notes: Reach for it on playful/organic briefs. The rounded terminals carry the whole mood; do not pair with another rounded face.

fonts.name: Oxygen
fonts.description: A clean, slightly humanist sans designed for the KDE desktop — crisp, efficient, and a touch technical. Light weight is elegant at large sizes.
fonts.notes: Only three weights — plan the hierarchy around 300/400/700. Good technical body face; less range for display than the variable sans.

fonts.name: Quattrocento
fonts.description: A classic wide old-style serif with generous counters and low contrast — traditional, calm, and very legible. Feels like a well-set book.
fonts.notes: Wide and sturdy — comfortable for body and dignified for headings. Two weights only; pairs with Quattrocento Sans if you want a matched sans.

fonts.name: Roboto
fonts.description: The ubiquitous neutral grotesque — mechanical skeleton, open curves, dead reliable. Invisible in the best way; gets out of the content's path.
fonts.notes: Maximum familiarity and legibility, minimum personality. Reach for it when the design carries the character and the type should just disappear.

fonts.name: Work Sans
fonts.description: A grotesque optimised for on-screen text at mid sizes — slightly quirky at display, calm and even in body. A flexible, contemporary neutral.
fonts.notes: A superb sans body partner for a serif display (Cormorant, Baskervville, Libre Caslon). Even texture in paragraphs; unobtrusive.
